issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' directly conflicts with marked memory disturbance items indicating fragmented, poorly integrated, repeatedly replaying trauma memory. While some patients can describe intrusive memories, 'very easily' is hard to reconcile with a profile centered on disjointed and involuntarily replayed recollection, so this is a clear within-node inconsistency.

This makes the maladaptive strategy items look disconnected from the endorsed memory and appraisal pattern rather than coherent trauma-related avoidance.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Verbal Access' directly conflicts with the combination of markedly fragmented/disconnected recall and repetitive involuntary replay. A patient may have intrusive replay or fragmented recall, but saying they can talk about the event very easily sits in tension with this memory profile and is hard to reconcile as part of the same self-report cluster.

issues.item: Memory: Fragmented Pieces: My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together.
issues.explanation: The avoidance items are not well anchored to the stated trauma type (mugging/robbery) or to the rest of the profile. Avoiding enclosed spaces and religious spaces lacks an evident connection to the reported memory and appraisal content, and these strategies do not cohere with the formulation, where Triggers are inactive and the strongest pattern is Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies. Screen-based distraction fits that pattern, but these specific place avoidances look clinically disconnected from the rest of the self-report.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.

A patient whose trauma memory is fragmented and repeatedly replays typically does not also report being able to talk about the event very easily; that is a direct within-node inconsistency.

These strategies appear disconnected from the cognitive formulation as well, because the active formulation centers Negative Appraisals ↔ Memory with strong influence on Maladaptive Strategies, yet the selected appraisals and memories do not plausibly lead to specifically avoiding enclosed or religious spaces.
